findings.summary: Case-sensitive matching hides identifying lines where a lowercase term is capitalized at the start of a line.
findings.evidence: A case-insensitive search for identifying lines in the scanned files finds BRIEF.md:713 '4. Planning: Surface missing interaction expectations when decomposing similar work.' This is a bullet in which the term opens the line and is followed by ':', exactly the plan's identifying form. Because the plan matches 'planning' case-sensitively, this line is never scanned for coverage. The plan's claim that the full set is BRIEF.md 11, 367, 411, 596 and 597 holds only because of case sensitivity. Fix: Match the first letter without regard to case when the term name starts in lowercase (planning, job, landed), so 'Planning:' and 'Job:' count. Keep proper names (Athena, Hermes, Sri) case-sensitive. Then cover BRIEF.md:713 with a sense, for example the pipeline-stage meaning of planning, or note in D152 why it is a separate use. Add a unit test for a capitalized identifying line.
findings.location: Plan decision 4 and step 2 (`name_hits`, `is_identifying`: case-sensitive); BRIEF.md:713

findings.summary: For the five terms with no identifying line (planning, job, landed, Sri, product versus system), the check compares the definition only with phrases the author chose. A new contradiction elsewhere in their sources would go unnoticed, and the plan does not say so.
findings.evidence: The only identifying lines are for Athena and Hermes (BRIEF.md 11, 367, 411, 596, 597). For the other terms, the obligation is at least one sense whose marker and `says` the author picks. The old planning error ('It is proposed, not built', docs/ontology.toml:22) would not have been caught by this check before someone wrote the 'hard jobs only' sense. The defaults rule 'mechanism' asks that any part a mechanism does not enforce be marked prose-only. Fix: In D152 and in the test header, state the limit plainly: the check guards the claims that senses list and the identifying lines; new drift in other source lines is not detected and is prose-only. Keep the design otherwise; classifying every line was rightly rejected.
findings.location: Plan decision 2 (coverage only on identifying lines) and D152 content

findings.summary: The per-term alteration removes exactly the `says` phrase the check looks for, so the test partly restates the check rather than showing a realistic wrong definition.
findings.evidence: The mutation is 'removing each sense's `says` from that term's definition'. This fails without `claim_problems`, but the altered input is built from the check's own data. The Hermes case is the only one built from a real fault: a tool-only entry with the role line BRIEF.md:597 uncovered. Fix: Also assert that the base (pre-change) definitions of planning ('It is proposed, not built.'), Athena (no studied-instance sense) and landed (no merged-unverified) are each flagged against the new senses. That shows the check catches the real disagreements this job corrects.

findings.summary: Two planning senses are weakly anchored or left unspecified.
findings.evidence: The sense {BRIEF.md, 'planning first', says 'Queue planning'} anchors on a heading (BRIEF.md:537 '### 2026-10-16: Speed, planning first, and initiatives in parallel'), and that line does not describe queue ordering. The sense {job-planning.md, 'a planner and a critic before the producer', ...} leaves `says` unspecified. Fix: Pick a `says` for the job-planning.md:1 sense, such as 'a planner and a critic'. Anchor queue planning on a line that describes ordering, or say in D152 that D105 is its real source and BRIEF.md:537 only records the misread.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot, and it fits the request and the accepted reading. It keeps the rejected job's approach (senses, excuses, scanning BRIEF.md and each term's file sources) and fixes each of that job's findings: excuses must be per marker and per file, and none are file-wide. It also adds the introspection's two requirements: every term needs a checked claim, and an altered definition must be flagged for each term. Everything the plan names exists: `problems`, `real_text`, `term`, `scratch_root`, `GOOD` and `repo_root` in crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs, and the seven terms in docs/ontology.toml. D151 is the last decision, so D152 is the right number. I searched the scanned sources for the plan's markers and found every one on a line that names the term: BRIEF.md 11, 193, 367, 596, 597, 1007, 1008 and 1009; job-planning.md 1 and 280; records.md 35; native-pr-landing.md 497 and 499. BRIEF.md:412 carries no 'Athena', but the plan's rule that adds the next line after a line ending in ':' covers it through 411. A case-sensitive search confirmed the plan's set of identifying lines. The demonstrations call the real `claim_problems` on the real files or on tempdir copies, and each would fail without the check. Nothing calls an external service, no athena.toml field is added, and the work fits one producer run. I found three soundness gaps, all minor: matching is case-sensitive, so it misses the identifying line BRIEF.md:713 ('4. Planning:'); five of the seven terms are checked only on phrases their author picks, which the decision should say plainly; and the per-term alteration test removes the very phrase the check looks for. None stops a criterion from being shown.
